lanes.title: Phase D design groundwork: caps and the mortar counted object, support capabilities, War Sandbox, deployment, economic scale
lanes.brief: Phase D design groundwork for DIR5 items the earlier lanes did not cover. Read first: docs/d079-m7-governance-reconciliation-2026-11-05.md §1.1 DR24, DR25, DR29, DR30, DR31, DR32, DR33; §4 D8 (the support-capability part only), D10, D15, D20; §1.5 readings R2, R5, R6, R7; §5 (Q3, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q14 stay OPEN; do not decide them); §6 'Not authorized by this record'. Also docs/d076-m7-decision-reconciliation.md §5 (CAP-1..CAP-5 rows) and docs/m7-plan/unit-catalogue-and-progression.md §4.5 (categories A-E; D-065 R8: a unit family is a controllable formation only). An earlier brief for this lane was lost with the old container; this brief replaces it. SCOPE LIMITS: work only in prototypes/m7-sprint1 (the isolated prototype: M7Proto.slnx, and M7Econ.slnx if economy code is touched) and docs/m7-plan; no change to Sim.Core, Sim.Data, Sim.Cli, Sim.Ui or their tests; no change to unit data or caps (D10: 'Nothing changes in data now'); no permanent project and no CI change. Every design document is marked PROPOSAL; every reading is labelled READING with both alternatives; no Director decision is invented or reopened. (1) CAPS AND COUNTED OBJECTS (DR24, D10). Write docs/m7-plan/caps-and-counted-objects-proposal.md: (a) a technical definition of the counted object for the mortar cap of 5 (for example the weapon system or tube with its crew, versus crew members, versus teams), with the alternatives, their consequences for data, battle entities, the AutoResolver and the economy, and one labelled recommendation; (b) the CAP-1..CAP-5 resolution strictly along D10's recorded basis (caps prevail over provisional TUNE personnel bands; CAP-1 and CAP-2 classing or retune options with attributed golden moves; CAP-3 V1 transient machines and a crew-per-machine TUNE rule; CAP-4 a category-A sniper identity distinct from 407 and a mortar identity classified A-E, created only in an authorized packet; CAP-5 no invented cap, READING R6 for vessels and drones, a performance cap proposed only if measured), citing each data row an option would touch (Sim.Data/content/unit-families.json by line) WITHOUT changing it; (c) an A-E classification of every new identity the lane names; (d) how the caps apply in the sandbox: DR30 'unrestricted experimental force creation' read against DR24 (READING, both alternatives). In the prototype, add a deterministic cap check at formation creation and edit (prototype constants citing DR24, not Sim.Data), with refusal codes and tie-dense tests; reuse lane N's CAP-5 treatment (reports/H-N.md: transports under 'Ships 5', crew-served guns uncapped) instead of redoing it. (2) SUPPORT CAPABILITIES (DR29, D8 support part). DR29: support units are primarily panel-managed capabilities, not battlefield entities; medics and supply wagons are examples and 'These figures are examples, not approved formulas'; morale decreases when troops take part in combat; support capabilities modify relevant effects; define stacking, allocation, costs, limits and formulas; never render them as battlefield entities. Write docs/m7-plan/support-capabilities-proposal.md and implement it in the prototype: the capability set (start from the DIR5 examples; any further capability is a labelled proposal), allocation from a panel to formations (per pulse or per battle: say which and why), deterministic stacking (diminishing or capped), limits, costs through the existing war-economy path (lane E, reports/H-E.md §2-§4: per-pulse settlement through Ledger.Flow/Ledger.Transfer, exact conservation), per-sim-year rates integrated with dtYears; what each modifies: medics act on the wounded/killed split or recovery inside the existing casualty and BattleOutcome mapping (Law 1 exact); supply wagons act on supply, ration or ammunition endurance inside the existing logistics path (lanes E and F; do not invent a second supply model); the morale-decrease-with-combat rule and how support modifies it, reusing the TacticalResolver's morale. Semantic tests per mechanism, exact conservation, tie-dense ordering tests, a POPULATED-table round-trip test for any new serialized row, and bounded mutants. (3) WAR SANDBOX (DR30, DR33, D15; DR31 reuse). Write docs/m7-plan/war-sandbox-proposal.md covering the modes (Quick Battle, Scenario Editor, Battle Test, Replay and Inspection; Campaign Encounter later) and implement the core in the prototype: a sandbox session isolated from campaign population and casualties, with the casualty accounting form under Law 1 (D15; for example a sandbox-scoped ledger whose minted forces and casualties never touch campaign accounts) and tests that a campaign world's state hash is identical before and after a sandbox battle and that sandbox totals conserve exactly; force creation from any designed unit family regardless of campaign era (DR33; campaign availability stays gated by computed Age, READING R2); terrain editing in the sandbox, refused for a loaded Campaign Encounter (it inherits campaign terrain); AI-vs-AI sandbox battles through the AutoResolver with no rendering (use lane P's model as it stands on the branch and say that its acceptance is OPEN, Q4); campaign resolver rules unchanged; deployment always through lane TR's DeploymentPhase (thirds, DR31; reports/H-TR.md §2 and P-TR5), with the editor's deployment zones bounded by the thirds (READING R5). Say, as a proposal only, how the two shipped scenarios that violate the thirds (parity Ambush and lane N Amphibious; reports/H-TR.md) are offered in the sandbox without normalizing realistic asymmetry (DR32). Replay and Inspection: deterministic replay of a sandbox battle from its order log, with a hash pin and a turn-exact order-delivery pin. (4) ECONOMIC SCALE (DR25, D20). DR25: 500-1,000 troops readily achievable, 50,000 difficult; recruitment and maintenance constrain scale; hard caps may protect performance, but ordinary scale is governed by the economy. Lane F measured that 50,000 is unreachable today (reports/H-F.md §7: the personnel predicate accepts at most 2,240-3,500 at turn 25 and 10,880-13,680 at turn 200). First re-measure the population trace on HEAD (D20, Q-L2) with the economy prototype; then write docs/m7-plan/economic-scale-proposal.md: which existing levers (recruitment cost, recurring maintenance, the personnel predicate, food and logistics) would make 500-1,000 readily achievable and 50,000 difficult, with measured evidence over several seeds and horizons; alternatives and consequences; no data change; the calibration itself goes through the ADR-055 amendment A-38 and M7.14 later. Do not choose the food-allocation ordering (DR27, Q3 OPEN): where a result depends on it, run both orderings and show both. (5) The lane report prototypes/m7-sprint1/reports/H-D.md: what exists; the designs; readings applied; the decisions the Director must take (only genuinely undecided ones, each with alternatives and consequences); MEASURED vs INFERRED; tests and mutants; what ran, what was NOT RUN and what was deferred. Builds and tests: M7Proto.slnx (and M7Econ.slnx if touched) in Debug and Release, prototypes/m7-sprint1/scripts/check-proto-determinism.sh, and python3 scripts/check-doc-links.py --all.
